question: Calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime, releasing a large amount of heat. This reaction is an example of which of the following types of reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A combination reaction occurs when two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
 
• In the given reaction, calcium oxide (CaO) reacts with water (H₂O) to form a single product, calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂).
 
• This reaction is highly exothermic, releasing a significant amount of heat.
 
• The chemical equation for this combination reaction is: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination Reaction:**

 
 
• Also known as a synthesis reaction, it involves two or more substances combining to form a single compound.
 
• Examples include the formation of water (H₂O) from hydrogen (H₂) and oxygen (O₂).
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction:**
 
 
• A reaction that releases energy in the form of heat.
 
• These reactions often occur spontaneously and result in an increase in temperature.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Oxide (CaO):**
 
 
• Also known as quicklime or burnt lime.
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline substance used in various industrial processes.
 
 
 
• **Slaked Lime (Calcium Hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂):**
 
 
• A compound formed by the reaction of calcium oxide with water.
 
• It is used in various applications such as water treatment, construction, and chemical manufacturing.
